Attention Trading Partners: the MaineCare Partner Portal is Live

Oct 12, 2026

As an update to previous communications, we have launched the new MaineCare Partner Portal, which replaces the previous HealthPAS Online Portal. The MaineCare Partner Portal is now available for all regular functions, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  

As a reminder, starting today, we are also changing how callers interact with and experience Provider Services and Member Services call center phone menus, known as Interactive Voice Response (IVR). A virtual assistant, called Gabby, will replace traditional phone menus by listening to what callers say to resolve simple inquiries. 

This message includes information you will need to get started in the MaineCare Partner Portal. The link to the MaineCare Partner Portal has not changed: mainecare.maine.gov. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the MaineCare Partner Portal section of the Provider Resources page. Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 21, 2026. For information about the claims submission deadlines for the October 15, 2026 and October 21, 2026, payment cycles, please refer to the FAQ. 

Migrated Trading Partner Account Admin (R7) users 

  1. Complete a one-time self-service password reset. Click “Sign In” within the MaineCare Partner Portal, then click “Forgot Password” to reset your password. The “Forgot your password?” feature is now a self-service tool! Provider Services will not be able to assist with password resets. 
  2. Set up a Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) method. 
  3. Sign into MaineCare’s Partner Portal. 
  4. Invite additional (delegated) users and assign permissions as appropriate. Refer to the MaineCare Partner Portal Overview User Guide in the MMIS Learning Center. 

Find step-by-step instructions and additional resources in the “ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance” course located in the MMIS Learning Center. 

Non-Migrated or New Trading Partner Account Admin (R7) users 

  1. Click “Register” within the MaineCare Partner Portal to complete a one-time registration, including setting up a password and an MFA method. 
  2. Invite additional (delegated) users and assign permissions as appropriate. Refer to the MaineCare Partner Portal Overview User Guide in the MMIS Learning Center. 

Find step-by-step instructions and additional resources in the “ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance” course located in the MMIS Learning Center. 

All other (delegated) users 

  1. Please contact your Admin (R7) user if you have not received an invitation to the MaineCare Partner Portal. You will receive an email link to register. This email will come from MEMMISDoNotReply@gainwelltechnologies.com. 
  2. Enter your invitation verification code, create a password, and set up an MFA method.  

Training Courses and Resources 

All training courses and resources are available through the MMIS Learning Center; refer to the ME LMS Student User Guide you received when you registered for training for instructions on how to access them. The same resources are also available in the MaineCare Partner Portal under the Provider tab > Provider Manuals subtab.

System Remittance Advice (RA) and 835 Limitations

Oct 13, 2026

Attention Nursing Homes, Hospitals, and Private Non-Medical Institutions, Appendix C & F (PNMI-C-F): Claims RA/835 Issues

Following the MIHMS upgrade, there are open issues affecting some RA/835s.  The issues are high priority for a fix that is underway; we are currently targeting to fix the issues by the end of October and will send another communication when the issues have been resolved. This message provides details of the issues and available workarounds until the issues are fixed. 

Cost of Care Reporting for Nursing Home, Hospital Claims, and PNMI-C-F 

Nursing Home and Hospital claims for members with cost of care are not being reported with the appropriate Claim Adjustment Reason Code (CARC) needed for balance billing members. 

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for cost of care. 
  • 835 – CARC 96 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the Dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Cost of Care Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Spenddown Reporting for Provider Claims 

Claims with spenddown are not being reported with the appropriate CARC needed for balance billing members. 

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for spenddown claims.   
  • 835 – CARC 96 and/or CARC 178 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Spend Down Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Hospital Crossover Claims 

Hospital crossover claims are not reporting the correct CARC when the member has Medicare and full MaineCare coverage, and the claim balance is for deductible or coinsurance.  In this situation, you would normally expect a B1 CARC. 

  • PDF RA – CARC B1 is being reported appropriately. 
  • 835 – CARC 45 is being reported in error. 

As a one-time workaround, MaineCare will provide a report after this issue has been resolved. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Bad Debt Write off Report.” We anticipate this report will be available by November 13, 2026, and will confirm once the issue is resolved. 

Claims Processed in Excess of Charges 

Claims processed in excess of billed charges are not being reported with the appropriate CARC. 

  • PDF RA – Reporting CARC 94 appropriately. 
  • 835 – Claims that pay more than the billed amount (i.e. FQHC, Hospitals with APC, DRGs) are reporting CARC 45 instead of CARC 94. 

MaineCare does not have a workaround for this issue, as CARC 45 and CARC 94 share the same Claim Adjustment Group Code of CO (Contractual Obligation). MaineCare can provide a report upon request; please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.  

For questions, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585.

The MaineCare Third Party Liability (TPL) Exemption Request and Attestation Form is Now Available

Oct 13, 2026

On August 3, 2026, MaineCare announced claims system updates to support proper TPL reimbursement processes in accordance with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Chapter I, Section 1.07 TPL rules. The MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form is now available for TPL exemption request submission.  

Requesting TPL Exemption 

In accordance with MBM, Chapter I, Section 1.07 rules, MaineCare may assess the validity of extenuating circumstance or service code TPL exemption requests to bill MaineCare as the primary payer for services delivered to a member with primary, public, or commercial coverage. Providers wishing to apply for TPL exemption to bill MaineCare as the primary payer must complete and submit the MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form to the TPL Medicare Code Exempt Request email box.  

MaineCare will review completed forms with the supporting documentation and provide a decision letter of approval or non-approval via email to the requestor. An exemption request approval letter is valid only for a specific member for a defined duration, no greater than 12 months. The exemption request approval letter must be attached to all applicable MaineCare claims for dates of service during the approved time. Claims without a valid and up-to-date approval letter may result in denials.  

Providers are responsible for maintaining exemption request renewals by submitting a subsequent MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form at least 30 calendar days prior to the expiration date specified in the approval letter.  

Limited Retroactive TPL Exemption Review Period 

For a limited time, MaineCare will consider continuity of care retroactive exemption requests with supporting documentation for claims directly impacted by the system updates announced in the Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing e-message we sent on August 3, 2026.  

After December 31, 2026, retroactive exemption requests may not be accepted for review. Providers who receive retroactive exemption request approvals may resubmit their claims with the applicable approval letter attached for claims processing. 

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

Federally Required MaineCare Off-Cycle Provider Revalidation Plan: October 2026 Update

Oct 13, 2026

As previously communicated, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) requested all states develop and submit a comprehensive two-year provider revalidation strategy, with priority given to revalidating high-risk providers. 

You can find Maine’s two-year plan and a list of all providers included in the off-cycle revalidation on the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) Federally Required 2026-2028 Off-Cycle Revalidation Plan webpage. OMS grouped providers into five cohorts and sends notices alerting providers at least 30 days prior to initiating the revalidation window for their assigned cohort. OMS additionally sends a 60-day post-initiation notice, per standard revalidation practices.

Milestones to note:

Cohorts 1 & 2: Individual high-risk providers, providers without an NPI, Personal Care Agencies, Home Health Agencies, Hospice, and Assisted Living Services providers

  • On July 19, 2026, OMS mailed a 30-day notice to impacted providers in Cohorts 1 and 2 announcing that their revalidation window would open on August 17, 2026.
  • Providers in Cohorts 1 and 2 who do not submit a revalidation case by Friday October 16, 2026, will have claims pend until they submit their revalidation case.
  • Providers who miss the October 16th deadline will have until November 16, 2026, to submit their revalidation case. Any provider who has not submitted a required revalidation case by that date will be terminated effective November 17, 2026.

You can find more information about the provider revalidation process on our Provider Enrollment and Revalidation webpage.

Questions?

For questions about this off-cycle revalidation process, please email Kenneth Jamison, Provider Enrollment Manager. For general assistance with the revalidation process, please contact the Provider Services Call Center at 1-866-690-5585, Option 7 for Revalidation Questions, or email MaineCare Enrollment.

The Department remains committed to program integrity, responsible stewardship, and clear communication with providers throughout this process. We will continue to share information with providers through usual communication channels as appropriate.

Reminder: Maine eCourts in Region 6 (Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County) Virtual Presentation Today at Noon

To help attorneys and other stakeholders in Region 6 get ready for eFiling, the Judicial Branch will hold a virtual presentation by Zoom today.

Passcode: 522889

The Zoom presentation will be recorded and posted on the Maine eCourts Training & Resources page following the live session.

District and Superior Courts in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo counties (comprising Judicial Region 6) will transition from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) on Monday, December 7, 2026. This includes all case types in the Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs) and Superior Courts; and in the Belfast, Rockland, West Bath, and Wiscasset District Courts.

Who Is Required to eFile?
Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

For more information about Maine eCourts visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

Please have this information ready before you call so that you can quickly provide it to Gabby. Gabby will prompt multiple times for the information it needs to proceed. If you do not provide a valid response, Gabby will disconnect. 

Once your information is validated, Gabby will guide you through additional prompts to help you obtain the information you need. 

If your inquiry is not related to one of the self-service options listed above, tell Gabby "other" to connect with a customer service representative for further assistance. You can ask to speak to customer service representative or agent at any time.

As a reminder, in addition to calling Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585, you can also email MaineCareprovider@gainwelltechnologies.com. For MaineCare Partner Portal issues, you can email MaineCaresupport@gainwelltechnologies.com.

The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors. The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF. At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. Additionally, the following websites are unavailable: bnc.uscourts.gov bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov notices.uscourts.gov National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.

item.title: US Department of Labor awards more than $10.5M in grants to support mine safety, health training across the nation
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor announced today that its Mine Safety and Health Administration has awarded more than $10.5 million in grants to reduce mining accidents, injuries, and illnesses by supporting training and education programs.The agency is awarding these grants to support the delivery of federally mandated training for new and experienced miners at surface and underground coal and metal and nonmetal mines. MSHA is awarding grants in 45 states, the Navajo Nation, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.“Thanks to President Trump’s leadership we’re investing billions of dollars into critical mining projects and resources for mining education,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “Today’s grant announcement furthers the Department’s goal to expand mining across the United States to support this Administration’s goals to provide critical resources to the workers industries that continue to expand in America.”States and territories apply for grant funding, which is then awarded to state mine inspectors’ offices, state departments of labor, and state-supported colleges and universities. Training and education programs are tailored locally to address conditions and hazards miners may experience.“A strong and thriving America relies on a mining industry that safely produces the minerals essential to our economy,” said Assistant Secretary for Mine Safety and Health Wayne Palmer. “These grants will promote safe and healthful workplaces for over 300,000 miners across 47 states, territories, and tribal lands.”Learn more about MSHA.The recipients of MSHA State Grants are as follows: RecipientCityState/TerritoryAwardBevill State Community College JasperAL $243,711University of Alaska at FairbanksFairbanksAK $160,886Arizona State Mine Inspector’s OfficePhoenixAZ $453,633Navajo Nation Minerals DepartmentWindow RockAZ $46,430Arkansas Department of Labor and LicensingLittle Rock AR $138,903Central Connecticut State UniversityNew BritainCT $98

item.title: Hours of Service of Drivers: Association of American Railroads and American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association; Application for Exemption Renewal
item.description: FMCSA announces its final decision to renew and modify the exemption granted to the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association and member railroads (the Associations) from the hours-of-service (HOS) prohibitions against driving after the 14th hour after coming on duty (the 14-hour rule) and against driving after accumulating 60 hours of on duty time within 7 consecutive days, or 70 hours of on duty time within 8 consecutive days (the 60-hour/70-hour rule). The exemption will enable covered drivers to respond to unplanned events that occur outside of, or extend beyond, their normal work hours. FMCSA modifies the previous exemption to limit the categories of unplanned events during which the exemption may be used and to add reporting requirements. In addition, only drivers operating for motor carriers listed in the Appendix to this decision may operate under the exemption. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and has determined that the exemption renewal, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.

item.description:
MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT Reporter of Decisions Decision: 2026 ME 103 Docket: Fra-25-550 Argued: September 8, 2026 Decided: October 22, 2026
Panel: STANFILL, C.J., and MEAD, CONNORS, LAWRENCE, DOUGLAS, LIPEZ, and TAUB, JJ.
DARBY SABIN
v.
SHAWN D. NEWCOMB et al.
CONNORS, J. [¶1] Darby Sabin appeals from an order of the Superior Court (Franklin County, Mills, A.R.J.) dismissing her complaint against Shawn Newcomb, Cynthia Soucy, and Owen Soucy. After careful review, we hold that Darby’s 1 complaint sufficiently alleges a claim for tortious interference with an expectancy of inheritance. We therefore vacate the dismissal and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
1 Due to the shared last names of multiple parties, we refer to them throughout by their first names. 2 I. BACKGROUND A. Factual History [¶2] The following facts are drawn from the factual allegations in the complaint, and, at the motion to dismiss stage, these allegations are viewed in the light most favorable to the plaintiff. See Meridian Med . Sys. LLC., v. Epix Therapeutics, Inc., 2021 ME 24, ¶ 2, 250 A.3d 122. [¶3] Steven Sabin, whose estate is at issue here, had three children: Paul, Kelly, and Janice. Paul predeceased Steven, leaving behind one daughter, Darby. Steven also had two stepchildren, Shawn and Cynthia. [¶4] In early 2022, as Steven and his wife, Christine, began experiencing cognitive decline , Steven executed a will and a �inancial power of attorney (“POA”). The will nominated Janice and Shawn as joint personal representatives and provided that Darby would receive what would have been Paul’s share of the estate.2 The POA appointed Shawn as Steven’s agent and granted Shawn a signi�icant range of authority. Among Shawn’s powers were the ability to transfer, revocably or irrevocably, any real, tangible, or intangible property. The POA further granted Shawn the power to give any property to any per
